# Feedback in interview when running LLM

**Headline:** `wl interview <id>` (the Herdr `r-i` shortcut) blocks silently for up to 15s when it makes an LLM request and no deterministic clarifying questions exist. Add console progress feedback — a "Thinking…" status message plus a TTY-only spinner — for every LLM call the command makes, and a brief fallback notice (not mentioning "local") when the LLM is unavailable, times out, or errors.

## Problem Statement

When `wl interview <id>` holds no outstanding parseable questions, it issues an LLM request (question extraction under `--llm`/`interview.intelligent`, or the producer-review explanation for a flagged item with no section/questions). Both run with a 15s timeout and print nothing while in flight. In the Herdr `r-i` pane the operator sees a frozen screen and cannot tell whether the command is working, hung, or finished.

## Users

- **Producer** running the `r-i` interview shortcut inside Herdr, who needs to know the command is doing work during a multi-second LLM request.
- **CLI operator** running `wl interview <id>` in a terminal or pipe, who needs the same feedback without polluting machine-readable output.

### Example user stories

- As a **producer**, I want the interview command to show a "Thinking…" indicator while it consults the LLM, so that I do not assume it has hung and interrupt it.
- As a **CLI operator** piping output, I want the status feedback to degrade to plain text (no spinner control characters), so that captured/piped output stays clean.
- As a **producer** whose LLM is unavailable or slow, I want a clear notice that structured evidence was used instead, so that I understand how the answer was produced.
- As a **script author**, I want `wl interview --json` to remain byte-for-byte valid JSON with no progress output, so that automation is unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Before every LLM request issued by `wl interview`, the command prints a static console status message (e.g. `Thinking…`); this covers both the LLM question-extraction fallback (`--llm` / `interview.intelligent`) and the producer-review explanation path.
- [ ] While a request is in flight and `process.stdout.isTTY` is true, an animated spinner is shown and is cleared before any subsequent output or interactive prompt is written; when stdout is not a TTY, no spinner/control characters are emitted (only the static message).
- [ ] When the LLM is unavailable, times out, or errors and the command falls back to structured evidence, the console prints a brief notice that does **not** contain the word "local" (e.g. `LLM unavailable — using structured evidence.`), and no spinner/status remains on screen.
- [ ] In `--json` mode the command prints no status message and no spinner — stdout remains valid JSON.
- [ ] When the deterministic parser finds clarifying questions, no LLM request (and therefore no status/spinner output) is produced.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the feedback helper for both TTY and non-TTY paths, and command-level tests assert the status message appears before each LLM call, the spinner is suppressed when non-TTY and in `--json` mode, and the fallback notice is printed on unavailable/error/timeout.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline. CI/CD pipeline tests are excluded.

## Constraints

- **No new runtime dependencies** — implement the spinner with `setInterval`/`process.stdout.write('…')` (or equivalent), consistent with the repo's existing dependency-free console output.
- **Output safety** — never emit ANSI/control sequences when stdout is not a TTY; never interleave spinner frames with the shared readline prompt or the `(y/N)` clear prompt.
- **Suppress in `--json`** — the JSON contract (`wl interview --json`) must remain untouched.
- **Preserve fallback semantics** — availability checks and silent structured-evidence fallback remain unchanged apart from the added notice; the notice must not mention "local".
- **Single shared prompt loop** — feedback must stop cleanly before `promptLoopFactory()` prompts are issued.

## Existing State

- `src/commands/interview.ts` prints a header summary, then:
  - calls `runInterview(...)` which, when the deterministic parser finds no pairs and `llmFallback` is enabled with an available client, calls `extractQuestionsWithLlm(...)` (`EXTRACTION_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000`);
  - calls `explanationFor()` → `buildProducerReviewExplanation(...)` (`EXPLANATION_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000`) for flagged no-section/no-questions items.
  - Neither prints any in-flight feedback.
- `ChatClient` exposes a synchronous `available` flag (`src/lib/llm.ts`); `buildProducerReviewExplanation` and `extractQuestionsWithLlm` currently swallow all failures and return a fallback/empty result with no success signal.
- `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` captures `console.log` output and injects `chatClientFactory`/`promptLoopFactory`, giving a ready seam for assertions.

## Desired Change

1. Add a small, dependency-free progress-feedback helper (co-located in `src/commands/interview.ts` or a reusable `src/lib/` module) that:
   - prints the static status message;
   - starts a TTY-only animated spinner on the same line;
   - stops and clears the spinner deterministically (on success, failure, and abort) before any other output.
2. Wrap every interview LLM call with this helper:
   - the LLM question-extraction fallback inside `runInterview` (e.g. via an `onLlmStart`/`onLlmSettled` callback hook in `InterviewRunOptions`, keeping `runInterview` IO-injectable and unit-testable);
   - the producer-review explanation call site in the command action.
3. Surface whether the LLM path was actually used so the fallback notice can be printed. Either extend the explanation path to report success (e.g. a companion function returning `{ text, usedLlm }` while keeping `buildProducerReviewExplanation` backward-compatible) or inject a callback; print the notice when the client is unavailable or the call failed/timed out.
4. Gate all feedback behind `!jsonMode`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/interview.ts` — add the progress helper, wire it around the extraction and explanation LLM calls, add the fallback notice, gate on `--json`.
- `src/lib/llm.ts` — only if a success signal must be threaded through; otherwise unchanged.
- `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` — new tests for the helper (TTY/non-TTY) and command-level feedback assertions.
- `README.md` / `CLI.md` — document the new interview progress feedback.
- `docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md` or the interview docs — update if the command's console contract is described.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MUUAMP7M008Z4GK** — "r-i interview explanation does not state why an item needs producer review" (completed): introduced the producer-review explanation LLM call this item adds feedback around.
- **WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF** — "interview: LLM-assisted question extraction as fallback" (completed): introduced the extraction LLM path. Its AC5 documents *silent* degradation; this item adds a brief user-facing notice while keeping the behavioural fallback silent.
- **WL-0MS7MFILJ0079283** — "Visible command execution pane for !/!! prefixed commands" (completed): explains why `r-i`'s `!!wl interview` output appears in a visible Herdr pane.
- **WL-0MKXK36KJ1L2ADCN** — "Enhanced OpenCode Progress Feedback in TUI" (completed): precedent for progress-feedback UX in this project.
- **WL-0MS6341OE008KWF2** — "Add error feedback in Herdr plugin UI when commands fail" (completed): precedent for surfacing command state to the operator.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Spinner/prompt interleaving risk:** the shared readline prompt loop may render over spinner frames; mitigation is to stop/clear the spinner before `prompts.next(...)` and before `defaultClearPrompt`. Covered by an AC.
- **TTY-detection risk:** Herdr panes may or may not report `isTTY`; the static message is the guaranteed baseline when the spinner is suppressed.
- **Fallback-signal risk:** `buildProducerReviewExplanation` currently gives no indication of whether the LLM was used; threading a success signal is required for the notice. Scope this to the interview call sites — do not change the function's public behaviour beyond an additive signal.
- **Scope-creep risk:** this item is limited to `wl interview`. Applying progress feedback to other LLM-using commands (embeddings, audit explanations) is explicitly out of scope and should be raised as a separate work item if wanted.
- **Assumption:** the fallback notice wording avoids "local" per producer direction, while remaining neutral about provider.
- **Assumption:** no new runtime dependencies are acceptable for the spinner.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which LLM-backed operations should show console progress feedback?" — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **Both** LLM paths — the producer-review explanation and the `--llm` question-extraction fallback.
- Q: "What should the console show while the request is in flight?" — Answer (producer, interactive reply): a static status message (`Thinking…`) **and** an animated spinner (TTY-only).
- Q: "When the LLM is unavailable / times out / errors and the command falls back, should the console say so?" — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **Yes**, print a brief notice, but do **not** mention "local".
- Constraint confirmed by agent (producer did not object): feedback must be suppressed in `--json` mode so stdout remains valid JSON.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSGEA9AY0080V4Q** – herdr plugin md viewer fails: Key Files paths resolved against plugin CWD, not worklog root (completed)
- **WL-0MLGBAKE41OVX7YH** – Async labels and listing helpers (completed)
- **WL-0MODFKH0C0006GB6** – Improve progress feedback for 'wl github import' (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: abort, ac5, acceptable, acceptance, action (+288 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: abort, action, add, added, adds (+262 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: abort, ac5, action, actually, add (+244 more)

# `wl close` lost-update: concurrent `wl sync` clobbers an in-flight close (item stays in_review)

Concrete instance of the store-lock lost-update gap tracked by WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7
(audit remaining mutating commands). The earlier fix (WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1) locked
`wl update`, `wl comment add`, and `wl audit-set` on the per-store file lock held by
`wl sync`; **`wl close` was not audited** and still performs an unlocked
read-modify-write.

## Problem

`wl close <id> --force` creates the close comment and sets
`status=completed`/`stage=done`, but does not hold the store mutation lock across that
read-modify-write. When a `wl sync` runs concurrently, its own load → merge → write-back
window can overwrite a `wl close` that commits inside it. The item reverts to
`completed`/`in_review`, its close comment is dropped, and `updatedAt` is left at its
pre-close value. The `wl close` process still exits 0 (`success: true`), so callers
believe the close happened.

## Evidence (ToneForge release v0.1.2, 2026-10-06)

The ship release close step (`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`, which shells out to
`wl close --force --reason "Shipped in v0.1.2"`) reported closing 53/53 items, but only
**50** persisted as `completed`/`done`. Three were reported closed with a success exit
code yet remained `completed`/`in_review`, with no close comment and unchanged `updatedAt`:

| Item | Title | State after release |
|---|---|---|
| TF-0MUUC9RTU008UJ18 | Add CLI command to register new primitive recipes | completed/in_review, updatedAt 2026-10-06T21:11:16Z (== auditedAt) |
| TF-0MUUELBUD002OEQ8 | Repair main checkout node_modules symlink loop blocking npm/vitest | completed/in_review, updatedAt 2026-10-06T21:11:54Z |
| TF-0MMZIW9NQ09MV98G | Convert hard-coded recipes to ToneGraph configs | completed/in_review, updatedAt 2026-10-06T21:12:03Z |

All three had `auditResult.readyToClose === true` and `needsProducerReview === false`, and
re-running `wl close --force` on a **copy** of the store closed them cleanly — confirming a
transient lost update, not a data/content problem.

Timing (worklog data ref `refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data`):

- Close loop wrote the 50 surviving items across 2026-10-06T21:33:33Z–21:33:52Z.
- A **delta** sync commit (`e993d47`) was created at **21:33:50Z — mid-loop**.
- The next full sync snapshot (`a0fc4c9`, 21:35:53Z) shows the three items still `in_review`
  with their close comments absent.

The three affected closes all committed inside the sync's load→write-back window; items
closed before or after it survived — the signature of an unlocked cross-process
read-modify-write, not a merge-preference issue (`wl sync` prefers the newer `updatedAt`,
so a committed, newer close would otherwise win).

## Desired behaviour

1. `wl close` (including the recursive/`--force` descendant loop) holds
   `withStoreMutationLock` across its whole read-modify-write, exactly as `wl update`,
   `wl comment add`, and `wl audit-set` now do.
2. A concurrency regression test reproduces the gap: a `wl close` interleaved with a
   `wl sync` load→write-back must leave the item `completed`/`done` with its close
   comment intact.
3. No behavioural change to close semantics otherwise; existing close tests pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl close` acquires the store mutation lock for the duration of the close (comment +
   status/stage update + any recursive descendant closes).
2. A regression test proves a close that lands during a concurrent `wl sync`
   read-modify-write is not lost (item remains `completed`/`done`, close comment present).
3. Existing `wl close` tests and the full suite pass.

## Notes

- Parent umbrella: WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7. Original lost-update fix: WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1.
- Related: WL-0MQ057APG009I7IJ (intermittent removal of recorded audits during `wl sync`),
  WL-0MQQJDQ7M000X2L4 (`wl close` silently orphans children when no audit result exists).
- The caller-side robustness gap (the ship skill trusting `wl close`'s exit code without
  verifying persisted state) is tracked separately in SorraAgents (SA-0MUX8PYAY0008HFZ,
  being refiled there as a ship-side verification guard).
